title: Pre-retry log line prints unreadable floating point delays
title_original: Apply formatting to num seconds in before_sleep_log
text_rewritten: The log line emitted just before each backoff pause interpolates the delay straight into the message, so a combined wait strategy produces entries like 'Retrying … in 0.30000000000000004 seconds as it raised …'. That is noise in every log aggregator we run, and because each line is textually unique it defeats grouping entirely. The equivalent post-attempt log helper already lets us pass a format for the seconds; the pre-sleep one does not. Please render the delay as a readable number by default and let callers override the rendering with the same kind of `sec_format` option the post-attempt helper accepts. The rest of the line — the function name, the 'raised …' / 'returned …' clause, and the exception-info plumbing — has to stay exactly as it is, because we parse it.

acceptance_hint: A combined wait of 0.1 + 0.2 logs 'in 0.3 seconds' by default, a supplied `sec_format` such as `%.2f` renders 'in 0.30 seconds', and the remainder of the message is byte-for-byte what it was.
